package_info.why_malicious: The package contains hidden code that disrupts web applications by deleting files on the victim's machine if the code is used outside of an allow-listed set of domains, effectively acting as a kill-switch or sabotage mechanism against unauthorized users.

execution_context.file_location: main application code (likely index.js or a core module of the package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if the application is running on an allow-listed domain (e.g., vue-admin-beautiful.com), and if not, it deletes project files from the filesystem, causing application disruption or data loss.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Code that deletes files based on the runtime environment is highly destructive and not expected in legitimate packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not perform destructive actions like deleting user files based on the domain or environment in which they are run.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Self-destruct or kill-switch logic is sometimes used in DRM or anti-piracy software, but is never appropriate in open source or general-purpose npm packages.
key_indicators: Domain-based conditional logic for destructive actions
Use of filesystem APIs to delete project files
Hidden or obfuscated code to evade detection

attack_chain.action: User installs or runs the package in their web application.
The code checks if the application is running on an allow-listed domain (e.g., vue-admin-beautiful.com).
attack_chain.leads_to: If not allow-listed, destructive action is triggered.

attack_chain.action: If the domain is not allow-listed, the code deletes project files, disrupting the application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Application is sabotaged or data is lost (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: Runtime domain/environment checks followed by destructive filesystem operations
Conditional file deletion based on window.location or process.env
Obfuscated or hidden logic that triggers only outside of specific domains
file_indicators: References to fs.rmdirSync or similar destructive filesystem APIs
Conditional checks against window.location.host or process.env variables
Unusual code in main entry points (index.js, main.js) that is not documented
network_indicators: No direct network exfiltration, but checks for specific domains (e.g., vue-admin-beautiful.com) in runtime logic
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for code that performs destructive filesystem operations (such as fs.rmdirSync, fs.unlinkSync) conditionally based on the runtime domain or environment. Flag packages that contain logic to check window.location.host or process.env and then delete files if the environment does not match an allow-list. Review obfuscated or undocumented code in main entry points for hidden kill-switches or sabotage logic.
